full_judgment: 15. The Appellate Court, the last Court of fact, concurred with the above findings of the trial Court and gave further finding that recording of the suit land in the name of Museb Ail and others was wrong, because the Khadem of a Mosque is a servant, so the recording of their names as possessors was wrong; that when from the time immemorial, prayers were offered in the Mosque, the land on which the Mosque was situated could not remain in the name of an individual as possessor. The Appellate Court further found that as per paragraphs 218 and 188 of the Muhammadan Law, every Muhammadan was entitled to enter into a Mosque dedicated to God and since the prayer was offered to the Mosque situated on the suit land, the same became a waqf property. Therefore, the plaintiffs could not have any exclusive right on the Mazar and the Mosque. The Appellate Court found that the certified copy of the agreement dated 6-3-1922 (exhibit-2) not being 30 years old (certified copy of the kabala was obtained on 23-8-1973), no presumption of correctness could be attached to the said document. The Appellate Court further found that the suit was defective as the same was filed without serving any prior notice upon defendant No. 4, Chairman of Austagram Union Parishad in compliance with the provisions of bidhi 74 of the Union Parishad Manual, 1983 (it would be section 78 of the Union Parishad Ordinance, 1983) which mandated the prior service of notice to the concerned Chairman of the Union Council before filing a suit. The Appellate Court further observed that in Bangladesh, for every Mazar and Mosque, a committee was there and those were being run and managed by the committee, so the case of the plaintiffs that the Khadems of the Mazar and the Mosque shall have the exclusive right to manage thereof was not acceptable.
